entry.title: The First Integrated Circuit Was Built in 1958
entry.summary: Almost everything that makes the modern world hum, from the phone in your pocket to the sensor on a factory floor, traces back to a single quiet afternoon in a nearly empty laboratory in Dallas. In the summer of 1958, a newly hired engineer named Jack Kilby built the first working integrated circuit at Texas Instruments. It was a crude little thing, a sliver of germanium with a few components and some fine gold wires, but it carried an idea that would reshape electronics: that an entire circuit could be made from one piece of semiconductor material. Every microcontroller and connected device we build today is a descendant of that prototype. Kilby had only just joined Texas Instruments and had not yet earned any vacation time. The AI Agent Habit That Was Quietly Wasting My Time and Tokens
Tags: ai, localai, machinelearning, productivity, agents I realized I had been using AI agents in a way that looked smart but was actually pretty wasteful. The problem is that if you keep asking the agent to rediscover the same process over and over, you are paying for repeated reasoning, repeated tool usage, and repeated trial and error.
